questions.question_text: Triangular numbers count dots in growing triangles: 1, 3, 6, 10, ... What is the sixth triangular number?

questions.question_text: A mixture contains iron nails, sand and salt. Which order separates all three sensibly?

options.text: Dissolve in water, then use a magnet, then evaporate the water
Use a magnet, then dissolve the salt in water and filter the sand, then evaporate the water

questions.explanation: A magnet removes the iron first while the mixture is dry; a magnet can still pick out wet iron, so the order alone is not what makes the other options fail. Water then dissolves only the salt, filtering traps the sand, and evaporating the water recovers the salt. The dissolving-first option fails because it never filters: the sand stays in the mixture and ends up mixed with the recovered salt after evaporation. Evaporating a dry mixture does nothing, and strong heating does not separate the three.
questions.private_source_fit_note: Separation techniques are ch8; static asks iron filings + sulfur with a magnet, this adds a three-component ordered plan. Rev 7 corrected the explanation per integrator: magnetic removal works on wet iron too; the dissolving-first option fails because filtration is omitted, leaving sand mixed with the recovered salt.

questions.question_text: A solar year is about 365.25 days. If a calendar used exactly 365 days every year with no leap day, after 40 years the calendar would be off by about:
questions.explanation: Each year loses 0.25 day, so 40 x 0.25 = 10 days of drift. Leap years exist to stop this drift.
questions.private_source_fit_note: Leap-year reasoning is ch11; static asks why leap years are needed and a 3+1 cycle model, this quantifies drift.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question_text: In the food chain grass -> deer -> tiger, which level has the least total energy available to it?
questions.explanation: Energy is lost at each step as organisms use it for life processes, so the least energy reaches the top consumer, the tiger.
questions.private_source_fit_note: Energy decrease up a food chain is ch12; existing items read food-web arrows or name roles, none reason about energy transfer. Rev 4 reworked the trophic-level naming item.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question_text: A garden is sprayed with a chemical that kills most of its insects. What is the most likely first effect on the garden's birds that eat insects?

options.text: The birds increase because plants grow better
The birds' food becomes scarce, so their numbers may fall
Nothing changes, because birds do not depend on insects

questions.explanation: The birds depend on insects for food. Removing most insects makes food scarce, so bird numbers are likely to fall - one part of an ecosystem affects another.
questions.private_source_fit_note: Interdependence reasoning is ch12 topic 4. Rev 4 replaced the decomposer-recycler item (same proposition as reasoning2 and static items).

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter_title: Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
questions.question_text: Which set of conditions makes Earth suitable for life as we know it?

options.text: A very thin atmosphere and constant freezing cold
No water and strong solar wind on the surface
A surface covered only in dry rock
Liquid water, a suitable temperature range and a protective atmosphere

questions.explanation: Life as we know it needs liquid water, moderate temperatures and an atmosphere that supplies gases and shields harmful radiation.
questions.private_source_fit_note: Life-supporting conditions are ch13; static asks about liquid water and atmosphere separately, this combines them in one set.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter_title: Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
questions.question_text: A town wants to protect its local lake ecosystem. Which action would help most?

options.text: Treating sewage before it reaches the lake and keeping a green buffer of plants around it
Filling part of the lake for parking
Removing all fish to reduce competition
Letting factory waste flow in untreated

questions.explanation: Treating sewage stops nutrient overload and poisoning, and plant buffers filter runoff. The other actions damage the ecosystem.
questions.private_source_fit_note: Threats and protection are ch13; static has a city plan protecting a wetland, this is a fresh lake scenario.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: On a 1 cm square grid, a leaf shape covers 12 full squares and 6 half squares. What is the best estimate of its area?
questions.explanation: Count full squares fully and half squares as halves: 12 + 3 = 15 square cm.
questions.private_source_fit_note: Grid area estimation with full and half squares is an application of NCERT Ganita Prakash ch14 Area (hegp207, p149 unit full/fractional squares, p150 halves), https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/hegp207.pdf - an application of that method, not the textbook's exact leaf example. Rev 4 replaced the composite-subtraction item.
